findings.reason: §3/§4 must cite `_fleet_counts`, `_population_has_live_work`, `--exit-on-empty` and `--lifetime` as the mechanisms they extend, or the sections rebuild machinery that already runs.
findings.text: §3 proposes a per-session live roll-up that "reads the same live classification that crew(view='live') uses, and computes nothing of its own", but `_fleet_counts(snapshots, *, session=...)` already IS that computation: it partitions the fleet into working/blocked/unpromoted/waiting and narrows to a session via `_partition_session_rows` (reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:264), and every row already carries its output as the counter cell (`recovery_watch.py:1622` builds every transition with `_fleet_counts(running)`, rendered by `Ticker._stats` at reckon/crew/ticker.py:2138). Separately, the plan cites no prior art for §4 at all: `_population_has_live_work(project, *, session)` (reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:567) is exactly "does this session's own fleet still hold a run that has not ended", and `crew follow --lifetime DURATION` (reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:2214) already prints one final line naming the session's runs that need the coordinator — the end-of-follower line §4 reinvents. `crew watch --once/--exit-on-empty` (reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:2601) likewise already exits when no live pointers remain. `_session_host_child`/`_session_host_runs_follower` (reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:599) already read the host-child relation §4's "start a new child on the next request" depends on. The plan searched only `ticker.py` and the shipped `a-follower-row-is-worth-a-wake` contract; the other four mechanisms are absent from its text.

findings.reason: the section must either extend `_stats`'s cells (naming nodes there) or justify a second status block, else the row carries two overlapping reports of one fleet.
findings.text: §3 adds a compact roll-up ("a count, and the node of each") to the end of every printed row, but the row already ends with a counter block built by `Ticker._stats` from the same event counts, and those counts come from the same live classification `crew(view="live")` uses. The new block is a second rendering of the same population in the same row; the plan gives no reason the existing counter cells cannot be extended to name nodes instead of adding a parallel block.

findings.reason: the honest change is to extend `_population_has_live_work` and to supersede `DISPLAY` in place; two owners of "no live work" and two state-to-word tables drift apart silently, which is the failure the plan's own §5 argues against.
findings.text: §4 makes the follower child settle and exit when the session has no live run, re-deriving "no live work" logic that `_population_has_live_work` already owns for exactly this population. §5 compounds this: its seven-word table is proposed as "one table, owned in one place, which every surface that prints a run's state reads", yet the state-to-word owner already exists as `DISPLAY` (reckon/crew/ticker.py:298, consumed solely at ticker.py:884). The plan names neither owner.

findings.reason: the section must name `DISPLAY` and the counter bucket labels as retired or reconciled, per the interface-budget rule that an added family accounts for itself in its own text.
findings.text: §5 introduces a new state-word mapping table and adds to the public definition surface (public_definitions 1682, cli_options 349, mcp_views 34, refusal_families 23), and its own text says the run counters and §3's roll-up will read it, but it names nothing it retires or merges: `DISPLAY = {"completed_unpromoted": "unpromoted", "lane-event": "lane event"}` (reckon/crew/ticker.py:298) is superseded by the seven words and is left unnamed, and §3's bucket labels (`_WAIT_CELL = "queued"` with `_COUNT_FIELD = {"queued": "waiting"}`, ticker.py:365,371) must be reconciled with the word set. The plan neither retires the old table nor states why it must remain.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §5 puts one state-to-word table behind one mapping, and §3 reads that classification rather than deriving its own; no proposed module spreads behaviour across shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4 re-derives live-work/exit logic beside `_population_has_live_work` and the existing empty-exit path, and §5's seven-word table would sit beside the existing `DISPLAY` alias owner; both should extend the named owner rather than fork it.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1682, cli_options 349, mcp_views 34, refusal_families 23; §5 adds a state-word mapping table and states the run counters and §3's roll-up read it, but names nothing it retires — `DISPLAY` at reckon/crew/ticker.py:298 is superseded by the seven words and is not named.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites no existing mechanism for §3 (§2's row policy excepted): the per-session roll-up it "computes nothing of its own" for already exists as `_fleet_counts`, the settle predicate §4 needs already exists as `_population_has_live_work`, and the state-word table §5 adds already has an owner in `DISPLAY`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §3 adds a second per-row status block beside the counter block `Ticker._stats` already renders from the same live classification, without saying why the existing cell cannot carry the node names.
